description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian dish featuring tender chicken simmered in a rich, creamy tomato-based sauce. This beloved recipe balances subtle sweetness with aromatic spices, creating a truly irresistible culinary experience. Perfect for a comforting family meal or a special occasion, it pairs wonderfully with naan or basmati rice.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts

ingredients.notes: or Kashmiri chili powder for color
soaked in warm water for 15 mins

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with plain yogurt, 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder, 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours, for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Marinated Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is lightly browned and partially cooked. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the remaining 1/2 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, and 1/2 teaspoon coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Pour in the tomato puree or crushed tomatoes. Add the soaked cashews (drained) and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the tomatoes to cook down. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender to blend until completely smooth. Strain the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra silky texture, pressing solids through.

instructions.title: Combine Chicken and Sauce
instructions.text: Return the blended sauce to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the partially cooked chicken pieces back into the sauce. Stir well to coat the chicken. If the sauce is too thick, add 1/4 to 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth to reach your desired consistency. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until the chicken is fully cooked through and tender, stirring occasionally.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream, 1 tablespoon of butter, and the crushed fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi). Add sugar if using, to balance the tanginess of the tomatoes. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, ensuring the sauce is heated through but not boiled after adding cream. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve hot with warm naan bread, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For a truly authentic taste, marinate the chicken overnight. This allows the spices to deeply penetrate the meat, making it incredibly tender and flavorful.
Crushing Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms just before adding it to the sauce releases its unique aroma and is crucial for authentic Butter Chicken flavor.
Always add cream and final butter at the very end and avoid boiling the sauce afterwards to prevent the cream from splitting and maintain its velvety texture.
